# Review CHANGES REQUESTED for PAN-4436

# Review — PAN-4436
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — `configuration/session-vault.mdx` line 161 fails MDX compilation (`<machine>` outside a code span), so the published Session Vault docs page breaks (AC-10)

## Context
- Run ID: agent-pan-4436-review-48369f6d
- Manifest: /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-4436/.pan/review/agent-pan-4436-review-48369f6d/context.json
- Branch / workspace: feature/pan-4436 / /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-4436

- Base / prior cycle SHA: origin/main merge-base 5d500fb0d53 (PAN-4307 #4444 merged). The local `main` ref (9e82cde) is stale, so every diff in this review was taken against `origin/main`. No prior review cycle.

## Blocking Findings

### [requirements] User-facing Session Vault page no longer compiles as MDX — `configuration/session-vault.mdx:161`
- Severity: !
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect; in_pr_scope (WI-11 / AC-10).
- Trigger and changed-code connection: this PR added the paragraph "…marked "from <machine>". You can read them there…". In MDX, a bare `<machine>` is parsed as an opening JSX element. There is no closing tag, so compilation fails. The page is in the published navigation (`docs.json` line 108, `"configuration/session-vault"`).
- Expected / observed / impact: expected the page to render and tell the user where browse copies appear (AC-10). Observed: `@mdx-js/mdx@3` `compile()` throws `Expected a closing tag for <machine> (161:52-161:61) before the end of paragraph`. The same file on `origin/main` compiles cleanly. The Mintlify check shows `skipping` on the PR, so no CI job catches this. After merge, the Mintlify build fails or the page does not render, and the user-facing half of AC-10 is unmet.
- Evidence: a scratch probe in the session scratchpad installed `@mdx-js/mdx@3` and compiled both versions: `origin/main` → OK, branch → FAIL with the error above. CodeRabbit raised the same issue; this review reproduced it independently.
- Fix: put the placeholder in a code span, e.g. ``marked "from `<machine>`"``, or escape it as `<machine>`. Line 162's `` `pan vault resume <id>` `` is already inside backticks and is fine. After the fix, re-run an MDX compile of the page.

## Non-blocking Findings

1. **~ The service half does not isolate per-row DB errors (NFR-6 spirit)** — `src/dashboard/server/services/vault-browse-service.ts`, `refreshVaultBrowseCopies`. The engine (`browse.ts`) catches errors per record, but `upsert(copy)` and `remove(vaultId)` are called without a per-row `try`. One throw (for example `SQLITE_BUSY`) aborts the rest of that cycle's reconcile and skips the emit. The vault service's listener wrapper catches and warns, and the next cycle retries, so no data is lost. Wrapping each call and collecting failures would match NFR-6. FK coverage was checked: every FK into `conversations` is handled. `conversation_files` is deleted explicitly, `conversation_pull_requests` cascades, and the four self-references are nulled. So removal cannot fail on FKs.
2. **~ Validation gap: `VaultBrowseCopy.test.tsx` never runs in CI.** The root vitest config excludes `src/dashboard/frontend/**`, and `test:frontend-subset` (package.json line 135) is an explicit file list that does not include the new file. I ran it locally: 6/6 pass. Add it to the `test:frontend-subset` list so AC-8 stays guarded.
3. **~ The Playwright UAT spec is manual-only.** `src/dashboard/frontend/tests/pan-4436-vault-browse.spec.ts` is not in `test:playwright` (which runs only `command-deck-resource-strip.spec.ts`). The AC-9 evidence is the author's run, recorded in commits dac65d27cee and b8b925c2cba: the Command Deck path was used, and both screenshots were inspected against the style guide. I did not re-run it.
4. **? Orphaned decrypted files if the manifest is lost.** `browse.ts` removes files only for ids in the manifest. If `manifest.json` is corrupt or deleted, `readManifest` returns an empty manifest. A cache file for a record that was then tombstoned is never listed in `removed` and stays on disk as decrypted plaintext. Unarchived rows are still reconciled by the service; archived rows are not. This needs manifest loss first, so it is rare. A directory sweep of `browse/*.jsonl` against the kept set would close the gap.
5. **? Uncached browse query per list request.** `getConversationListWithVaultCopies` runs `listVaultBrowseConversations()` on every `GET /api/conversations`, while the local half is promise-cached. The cost is one indexed-table SQL query over a small row set, so the impact is bounded. Advisory only.
6. **Note:** a user retitle of a browse row is reverted at the next sync, because the upsert sees a title difference. This is consistent with "read-only copy" and needs no change.

### Reachability sweep (browse rows vs. other readers)
Every other `listConversations()` consumer inherits the exclusion: lifecycle poller, restart-all, settle poller, resource discovery, admin stuck list, attachments, heal, and resources. Raw readers were checked too. `correlator.ts` and ledger costs join through `conversation_files`, which browse rows lack. `conversation-cost-session.ts` matches `tmux_session` against an agent id. Transcript retention scans agent dirs only. Other frontend consumers of `/api/conversations` (CloisterStatusBar alive count, God View live filter) filter on `sessionAlive`, so browse rows do not count. `conversation.created` only bumps `conversationsListRevision`. Conversation names are never updated in place, so the name↔origin invariant holds.

### Four dimensions
- **Correctness:** one blocking docs defect; advisories 1, 4 and 6. The core data paths, reconcile logic and FK handling are correct.
- **Security:** vaultIds are regex-validated before any path use; removal has a containment check; files are 0600 and the dir 0700; nothing touches the deletion door; there is no new HTTP route. Record content comes from the same user's vault and renders through React. No findings.
- **Performance:** zstd decode is async; the refresh runs inside the vault queue, never on HTTP; `ended_at` is non-null, so the 2 s polling is not triggered. Advisory 5 only.
- **Requirements/UX:** AC matrix below. The badge and notice follow the style guide (existing classes, no pill or color), per the author's screenshot inspection.
